D007-D005_h001.question:
"It's been a rough stretch, doc. About seven months now, I think. Most days, I just feel… flat. Like my emotions are all turned down to zero. Even when I get a good fare, it doesn't really mean much to me. I used to feel satisfied, you know, proud of a long shift. Now? Nothing. And sleep, forget about it. I'm in bed for hours but I wake up feeling like I haven't slept a wink. I can't sit still either, got this constant urge to move, pacing around the apartment. It's gotten so bad I can barely focus on driving, which is my bread and butter.

Then, about six months ago, things got really strange. I started seeing things, little shadowy figures moving in my peripheral vision, mostly when I'm tired. And my ex-wife… I know she's with someone else, I just know it. I see signs everywhere, the way people look at me, whispers I hear when I'm out. It's frustrating because she denies it. But here’s the thing, even when those strange sights and suspicions about her infidelity started, and when they were all I could think about for a couple of weeks, that dull, empty feeling, the exhaustion, and the restlessness were still there, and they've been there pretty much constantly since this whole mess began."
D007-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h002.question:
It's been about seven months now that I’ve felt this overwhelming sadness, like a heavy blanket I can't shake off. I used to love the buzz of a crowded restaurant, the clinking of glasses, discussing vintages with patrons. Now, I dread it. Getting out of bed is a Herculean task, and then it takes forever to actually fall asleep. I feel my movements are so slow, like trying to walk through treacle.

Around six months ago, things got… stranger. I started to feel these creepy-crawlies on my skin, like bugs under my clothes, even when nothing's there. And I'm certain the world is ending. There's this growing darkness, a "void-rift," as I call it, that’s consuming everything. I’ve tried to explain it to people, but they just look at me blankly. It’s been happening alongside the low mood; it never felt separate. In fact, these bleak feelings have been with me for the majority of this whole difficult period. There was even a stretch of a few weeks where these unusual thoughts and skin sensations were happening even when my mood wasn't quite so low, before this awful sadness truly took hold.

I just can't function like I used to. The joy of identifying a perfect pairing, the nuances of a complex burgundy… it all feels utterly pointless when the world is about to disappear into a "chrono-sinkhole."
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h003.question:
It’s been almost seven months now that I’ve felt this dark cloud hanging over me. My husband tries to cheer me up, but even things I used to love, like gardening or even a good book, just don’t bring me any joy anymore. I drag myself out of bed in the morning feeling just as tired as when I went to sleep. The teachers at school must think I’m losing my touch; it takes me so long to even form a sentence sometimes when they ask me a question in meetings, and I can just feel the quiet pauses.

But then there are these other things, which started about six months ago. I keep noticing the smell of something burnt, like toast, even when there's nothing cooking. And it's odd, but I've become convinced that the superintendent, Mr. Davis, is secretly in love with me. He just looks at me in a certain way, and I know he's trying to send me messages through school memos. I've even caught myself speaking in rhymes sometimes, just making silly sounds instead of actual words.

I know it sounds strange, but for the past two months or so, I've had these intense beliefs about Mr. Davis and the phantom smells even when my mood isn't totally in the dumps; it’s like they were there on their own. But for the vast majority of these past months, this deep sadness has been constant. It’s making it so hard to lead my school; I just don’t have the energy or the drive anymore.
D007-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h004.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a rough stretch. I'm a 56-year-old divorced lawyer, and my mind just isn't what it used to be. For about seven months now, I've felt this deep sadness. I'll just start crying for no reason, and I can't seem to stop. Nothing interests me anymore. My golf clubs are gathering dust, and I used to love playing. At night, I'm constantly waking up, tossing and turning, and sometimes I just pace the house, wringing my hands, feeling this incredible restlessness.

But it's not just the low mood. For the past six months, things have gotten really strange. I'm convinced something's terribly wrong with my insides—I've seen specialists, but they say I'm fine. And the smells... I keep smelling this awful, rotting odor, even when there's nothing there. It's truly disturbing. When I try to explain it, my thoughts just jump all over the place. I know I'm not making sense, but my mind races from one idea to the next.

What's really difficult is that these dark, sad feelings, and all the bizarre things happening in my head, they've been going on at the same time. The strange smells and the belief about my body, those have actually stuck around even during the few times I've felt a tiny bit better and less tearful. But the depression, the sadness and the lack of interest, that's what's dominated almost the entire time I've been feeling ill."
D007-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h005.question:
"It all started feeling like a dark cloud descended around seven months ago, right after my husband passed. I just… couldn't even pretend to be interested in showing houses anymore. The energy was gone, and even the thought of making a sale and seeing a happy client felt completely meaningless. All I wanted to do was sleep, sometimes for twelve hours or more, and even then, I'd feel heavy and sluggish, barely able to move around the house. My movements feel like I'm underwater.

But then, about a month into that, things got really strange. There’s this client, a very distinguished gentleman, who I swear is sending me secret messages through the listings. I see him sometimes in the corner of my eye, standing in empty houses, just watching me with a look of profound affection. I know he’s madly in love with me, everyone can see it in his subtle gestures. These visions and beliefs have been consistent for the past six months, even during the rare times I might feel a flicker of something other than sadness. But the deep, hollow sadness and exhaustion... that's been the overwhelming constant, present almost every single day, for nearly the entire time these other experiences have been happening."
D007-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h006.question:
"Well, thank you for seeing me, doctor. It’s been… a really long time coming. My husband, he’s been urging me. For about a year and a half now, maybe a little longer, I’ve just felt this deep, hollow emptiness inside, like a void where my feelings used to be. Nothing makes me happy anymore. Selling a house, which used to be my passion, it’s just… bland. Food used to be a comfort, but even that’s gone. Half the time, I can barely swallow anything; it all tastes like sulfur and ash. I feel so guilty, doctor. I keep thinking, if I hadn't pushed so hard for that last commission, maybe the market wouldn't be collapsing. It’s my fault, I just know it.

And then there's the other stuff, which has been going on for over a year now. These thoughts just… jump around. One minute I'm talking about a property, the next I'm convinced the sky is falling, literally, and the world as we know it is ending. It's like my brain won’t stay on one track. These feelings, this emptiness and guilt, they’re almost always there, alongside these strange tastes and frightening ideas, for most of the time I’ve been feeling unwell. It's truly debilitating.

What really gets to me, though, is that even when I have a few good days, when the sadness lifts a bit, those thoughts about the world ending, and that terrible metallic taste, they just… linger. I mean, there have been weeks, even when I wasn’t feeling so utterly hollow, that those strange tastes and overwhelming feelings that everything is about to collapse were still very much present, without any of the other mood symptoms."
D007-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h007.question:
It all started about a year and a half ago, maybe a little more, after my wife passed. The emptiness just swallowed me whole, and I've barely felt connected to anyone or anything since. I stopped going out, even for a pint. I used to love talking to my regulars, but now the thought of it just makes me tired. I’ve lost a good bit of weight too, probably over 20 pounds, just haven't had an appetite.

Lately, though, things have gotten even stranger. For the past year and four months, I keep seeing things and hearing things. I see shadowy figures in the corners of my vision at the shop, like they’re watching me. And I just know, I *know* those health inspectors aren't just doing their job; they're out to get me, trying to shut me down for good. They’re involved with the police too, I’m sure of it. When my doctor asks me about it, I sometimes have trouble explaining exactly what’s happening, and I feel like I'm just rambling, going off on tangents. I even feel responsible for the accident down the street last week, like if I had just done something differently, it wouldn’t have happened. It wasn’t my fault, I know, but it feels like it. What's most confusing is that even when I'm not feeling so low, these visions and the feeling of being watched, they still happen. In fact, for about three weeks there, right in the middle of all this, I wasn't really depressed or anything, but those shadowy figures and the feeling of being targeted by the inspectors were still very much there, clear as day. And honestly, the depression has been here nearly constant since this whole nightmare began, even when the other things are happening, it’s like a heavy blanket that just won't lift.
D007-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h008.question:
"It's been a rough couple of years, doctor. I'd say for about a year and seven months now, I’ve just felt this emptiness, like there’s nothing inside. Things I used to love, like charting new courses or even just sitting with my wife, they just don't interest me anymore. I’ve put on a good bit of weight too, over five percent in a month, which is unusual for me. And the guilt… it’s overwhelming. I know it sounds crazy, but I feel like I'm to blame for every bad storm that hits the ocean these days, even the ones thousands of miles away.

About a year and four months ago, things got really strange. I started to notice that the news reports, even the commercials on TV, seemed to be directly talking about me, sending me coded messages. And I feel things, doctor, like a phantom touch on my arm or something crawling on my skin, even when there's nothing there. My thoughts jump around too; I'll be talking about navigation and then suddenly I'm on about the color of the sky, with no real connection.

What's really been troubling me is that these strange thoughts and sensations, they've been happening at the same time as this deep sadness. But what's important is, even when I'm at my worst with the voices and the odd feelings, I'm still bogged down by that crushing mood. Actually, there have been periods of a couple of weeks where those weird sensations and messages were still happening, even when the crippling sadness wasn't quite as intense, but still definitely lingering. The dark cloud of depression has truly been the constant companion through all of this, for most of this whole ordeal, to be honest."
D007-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h009.question:
"Well, for about a year and a half now, maybe closer to two, things have just been... off. It started with this heavy blanket of numbness. Nothing really brings me joy anymore; my old sailing logs, even the smell of the sea, it all just feels flat. I've put on a fair bit of weight, too, more than twenty pounds in a month, just not feeling like myself. And the guilt, doctor, it's crushing. I feel responsible for every storm that beaches a ship, even ones I'm nowhere near.

But more recently, over the last year and four months, things took a turn. I started feeling these crawling sensations on my skin, like tiny insects, even when there's nothing there. And I know it sounds mad, but I have this unshakable belief that certain crew members, they’re conspiring against me, trying to sabotage my vessel. My thoughts jump around erratically, too. One minute I'm talking about the tides, the next I'm on about the engine room, with no real connection.

The thing is, these strange beliefs and sensations started, but that heavy, empty feeling and the guilt, that was already there. And honestly, for the vast majority of the time these odd thoughts and feelings have been around, I’ve also been battling that deep, soul-crushing low. There were even a few weeks, perhaps a month, where I was just experiencing those strange crawling feelings and beliefs about the crew, but that really dark mood wasn't present at all."
D007-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h010.question:
I’m really struggling, doc. It's been over a year now, maybe a year and a half, since things started feeling off. I’ve just felt, well, empty. Like there’s nothing inside me. Even when I finish a big landscaping project, something I used to take pride in, I just don't care anymore. My appetite has actually gone up, which is weird, because I can barely get myself out of bed. I feel pretty worthless most days, like I'm a drain on everyone.

But then there are these other things that have been happening for about the last year and four months, some of them even longer than the emptiness. I keep smelling this metallic, burning smell, even when there's nothing there. And it feels like everything is… connected to me. Like the way people prune their rose bushes, or the patterns in the clouds, they’re trying to tell me something specific, just for me. It makes it hard to focus, like when you ask me a direct question, my mind just goes off on tangents, following these strange connections. The thing is, even amidst all these odd smells and secret messages, that empty, down feeling has been there for most of this whole time. In fact, for a good two weeks once, before I really started feeling so glum all the time, I was still smelling that burning and seeing those secret messages, but the deep sadness wasn't there. It’s mostly been the sadness though, for the longest stretch.
D007-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h011.question: It’s been, what, seven months now? Seven months of this… cloud. Before all this, I was a dermatologist, you know, a doctor. Now, it feels like the world is collapsing around me. I hear voices constantly, whispering about the end of everything, that a great catastrophe is coming, that it's all my fault. Sometimes they're so loud, I can barely focus. My own words often get jumbled, like a salad, and I find myself making these strange, repetitive gestures without even realizing it. Nothing brings me joy anymore; not my work, not my husband, not even a simple walk. I can't sit still; I pace, wring my hands, pick at my skin almost constantly. Every little thing that goes wrong, I somehow twist into my own doing, convinced I deserve to be punished. Sometimes I just wish it would all stop, that I could just disappear. These feelings, this profound sadness and lack of interest, they’ve been with me for the entire seven months of hearing the voices and believing in the end of the world. Even on the rare occasions the voices quiet down for a bit, or I’m not as convinced the world is ending, the darkness and inability to find any pleasure is still there; it truly defines how I've been feeling for most of this time. It’s hard to imagine ever feeling like myself again.
D007-D005_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h012.question:
Doctor, I… I don’t even know where to begin. For the past seven months, it’s been… a descent. The world, it feels like it’s going to end, truly. I smell this putrid, burning smell constantly, like everything’s rotting. Sometimes when I try to explain it to my wife, the words just… they don’t come out right. It’s like my thoughts are all scrambled, a jumble. And I find myself just pacing, back and forth, rubbing my hands, almost without realizing it. Even when I’m trying to lecture, I just… stop talking sometimes.

But it’s more than that. There’s no joy in anything anymore. Nothing. My lectures, my research, even spending time with my wife—it all feels flat. It’s hard to even move sometimes, like my body is heavy. I feel utterly worthless, like a burden. I’ve actually thought about how I could just… end it. I’ve even considered specific ways.

What’s so confusing is that these feelings, this absolute despair, and the other… oddities, they’ve been happening at the same time for months. This sadness, it’s just always there, a heavy blanket. But then, for a couple of weeks, even when the gloom lifts a little, or if I’m having an okay day mood-wise, those strange smells and the feeling that something terrible is coming, they still break through. That overwhelming sadness has been the main thing, though, dominating most of this horrifying period. It’s definitely affecting my ability to function at work.
D007-D005_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h013.question: It’s been, I guess, seven months now since things really started getting weird. I just feel… off. Like my insides are all tangled up. Sometimes, it feels like bugs are crawling under my skin, even when I'm just sitting here. My head is so foggy sometimes, I'll be talking and suddenly the words just rhyme, like, "My head is red, I'm feeling dread," and it makes no sense. I’ve probably lost most of my freelance clients because I just can’t focus on editing. And honestly, I don't even care anymore. The thought of going out, seeing friends... it just feels like too much effort. I’ll just sit and rock back and forth for hours. I even feel heavy, like moving is a chore. I look at my awards, my old work, and it's like none of it matters. I just feel utterly worthless. Sometimes I get these sudden urges, completely out of nowhere, to just run into traffic, or jump off my balcony, even though I don't really want to die. It's just a fleeting impulse. The hardest part is, these down periods, where I feel completely useless, they’ve been around pretty much constantly since this all started. But then there were these two weeks, a while ago, where I was feeling okay, not depressed at all, but those bugs were still crawling, and I was still convinced something was wrong with my organs. It's confusing.
D007-D005_h013.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h014.question:
"I'm here because my wife is really worried about me, and frankly, I'm starting to think she might have a point. Things have been... off, for about seven months now. I used to love flying, being up there, feeling like I had the world at my fingertips. But lately, it's just a struggle to even get out of bed. I feel worthless, like I'm not good for anything anymore. When people ask me something, it takes me forever to answer, and even then, my words just feel slow. I find myself just wishing I wouldn't wake up sometimes.

And then there are these other things. I hear voices, you know, not all the time, but enough to be unsettling. And I've gotten this profound sense that I am... chosen. I can understand the universe in a way no one else can, a cosmic pilot guiding the stars, like bells in the shell. These thoughts, they've been there consistently for the last seven months, almost the whole time I've felt so down. But sometimes, for a couple of weeks at a time, I’ll be having these big-vision thoughts and hearing things, even when I’m not stuck in the dumps feeling completely useless. It's really messed with my ability to connect with anyone, and my flying, well, it's just not happening anymore. I just can't bring myself to do much of anything."
D007-D005_h014.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h015.question:
It's been about seven months now. I just… I can’t get myself going anymore. Things I used to love, like trying new recipes or even just going for a walk, feel like too much effort. My body feels so heavy, like I'm moving through mud. And I feel so guilty all the time, for everything – for my divorce, for not being a better nutritionist, for just existing, really. Sometimes, I picture exactly how I could just… end it all, just to stop this feeling.

But that's not even the strangest part. For the past few weeks, there have been times when the depression eases a bit, but these other things happen. I keep seeing this beautiful yellow bird, just flitting around the edges of my vision, but then it's gone. And I just *know* my ex-husband, Mark, is still completely infatuated with me, sending me secret messages through the headlines of the newspaper – even though we haven't spoken in years. Sometimes, when this happens, my thoughts get really jumbled, and I'll say things that don't make any sense, almost like I’m a little kid again, giggling about nothing. It's almost impossible to talk when it's like that.

But even with those odd experiences, the sadness and slowness… that’s been the constant, overwhelming cloud for most of these past seven months, especially since the divorce. It’s like the other strange things come and go, but the dark, heavy feeling truly dominates almost every single day.
D007-D005_h015.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h016.question:
I don't know where to begin, everything just feels so heavy, all the time. For about ten months now, I've had this terrible emptiness inside me, like a hollow in my chest. I've lost a lot of weight, too, more than five percent of my body weight without even trying, and every night I’m plagued by these terrifying nightmares that wake me up in a cold sweat. Physical fatigue is constant; even the simplest tasks at home, like doing dishes, feel like running a marathon. It’s been tough to even get to work, let alone perform well.

The really bizarre stuff started about eight months ago, around the same time as this emptiness. I keep seeing things, usually shadowy figures lurking in the periphery of my vision, and sometimes even people who just vanish if I try to look directly. It’s unnerving. And everything seems to be about me, or at least that's how it feels. A nurse whispering in the hallway, a patient looking a certain way – it all feels like it has some secret meaning directed at me. I've also just lost all motivation; it’s a struggle to even get myself to do anything purposeful, whether it’s at work or just taking care of myself. This feeling of being utterly exhausted and empty has been present for most of the time I've been seeing and hearing these things, overshadowing everything else. Even when the visions and the thoughts about things being about me aren't as intense, this low mood and fatigue are still very much there, and have been for the majority of these eight months. There was a period of about three weeks, right after I first started noticing the whispers and shadows, where those strange experiences were really prominent, but I wasn't feeling as utterly hopeless or exhausted as I do now, or have been for most of this time. It’s confusing, but the depression and lack of motivation have definitely been the dominant problem throughout all of this.
D007-D005_h016.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h017.question:
It's been almost a year now, and I just feel... empty. Like a hollowed-out version of myself. Nothing interests me anymore. I used to enjoy my data entry, the precision of it, but now even that feels like a monumental effort. My husband tries to cheer me up, but I just can't summon the energy. I’ve lost a lot of weight, too, without even trying, probably because I’m so restless at night, waking up constantly. My brain just feels tired all the time, even simple tasks at work drain me.

And then there are these other things, which have been going on for about eight months. Sometimes I get this itching or crawling sensation on my skin, like bugs are there, but I know there’s nothing. And I’ve noticed people talking, on the TV mostly, and I know they’re sending me messages, sometimes about my work, sometimes just about my life. It's like everyone is in on some secret about me. What's even stranger is that these delusions and hallucinations keep happening even when I'm not feeling depressed, for weeks on end sometimes. But honestly, the depression has been the longest part of all of this, truly dominating most of the time these other odd experiences are happening. It feels like the sadness and lack of motivation have been with me for the majority of these past months, even when the crawling sensations and the coded messages pick up.
D007-D005_h017.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h018.question: It’s been a rough ten months, doctor. I just feel…heavy. Getting out of bed is a monumental task. My body aches, and every movement feels like I’m dragging lead. I’ve lost so much weight without even trying, my clothes are just hanging on me now. And sleep? I lie awake for hours, my mind racing. Then the voices start, whispering about my late husband, saying he was seeing other women right under my nose. It sounds absurd, he’s been gone for years, but they’re so persistent, and when I try to talk, the words just don't come out. It’s been this way for most of the eight months these voices and strange thoughts have been around. I just feel so low, day in and day out, and it’s made it impossible to even sit at my sewing machine anymore. The few times I've managed to push through, the voices are there, commenting on how I'm doing things wrong, and honestly, the thought of infidelity just keeps popping into my head, even about people from my past that it makes no sense for. It's been going on for so long, and it's making life unbearable.
D007-D005_h018.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h019.question:
I’m not sure where to start, doc. Things have been… off for nearly a year now, maybe ten months. I just feel so drained all the time, even after a full night’s sleep. And getting to sleep? That's a whole other battle. My wife, she says I'm like a zombie. I still eat, honestly, probably more than I used to, but it doesn't bring any pleasure. It’s like all my feelings have just… flatlined. I used to love my job as a firefighter, the camaraderie, the adrenaline, but now it’s just a blur.

The real trouble started about eight months ago. I began smelling burnt toast and smoke when there was nothing there, especially at work. Sometimes I'd hear things, or see flashes. Then, I started to notice that news reports, even just conversations on the radio at the station, they all seem to be thinly veiled messages about me, about my failures. I try to talk, but the words just get stuck. My wife keeps asking what's wrong, but I just… can't push them out. It’s like my mind is a blank wall.

What's really strange, though, is that even when those unsettling smells and thoughts are strong, and I feel completely out of it, that same empty, tired feeling is pretty much always there with me. It’s not like it comes and goes; it’s been the main thing for most of this whole ordeal, way longer than just the spooky stuff. And even when these ideas about the news and the smells are gone for a bit, that same low, numb feeling pretty much immediately returns. It feels like this deep emptiness has been present for the majority of the time I've been feeling this sick.
D007-D005_h019.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h020.question:
Lately, it’s been a real struggle just to get through the day. For about ten months now, I’ve felt this crushing fatigue that just won’t lift, no matter how much I try to rest. My appetite’s gone out the window too; nothing tastes good, and I’ve barely been eating. I wake up constantly throughout the night, and then I just lie there, staring at the ceiling and fighting back tears. It’s been so bad that I can barely function at work, and my wife is really worried.

Around eight months ago, things got even stranger. I started seeing things, like shadows moving in my peripheral vision, or brief glimpses of people who aren’t there. The oddest thing is this strong feeling that the woman who works at the coffee shop, the one with the brown hair, is secretly in love with me. She gives me a certain look, you know? Like she’s trying to tell me something, even though we’ve never really spoken. It's an intense feeling that she just adores me.

What’s really messed up is that for a good two weeks within the last eight months, when all this bizarre stuff was happening – the shadows and knowing about the coffee shop lady – I actually felt pretty normal emotionally. I wasn’t crying or feeling down at all during those two weeks; it was just the visual stuff and knowing about her. But most of the time since all this started, the depression has been the main thing, really dragging me down while all the other strange experiences are happening too.
D007-D005_h020.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D005_h021.question:
Lately, it feels like the world is playing a cruel joke on me. I’ve been struggling for well over a year now, closer to a year and seven months, and for most of that time, I’ve just felt this deep, unending sadness, like a heavy blanket I can't shake off. It's been nearly a year and six months of this gloom. I barely sleep, just toss and turn, my mind racing with thoughts, and I find myself constantly pacing or fidgeting, unable to stay still. Nothing brings me joy anymore; activities that used to light me up just feel… flat.

But it's more than just the sadness. For the entire time I've felt this way, strange things have been happening. I see things, fleeting figures in my peripheral vision, shadows that aren't there. And I hear whispers, sometimes they tell me things about these "special reports" on the news that are clearly meant for me, decoded messages about my work, my influence. People are talking about me, subtly, through their actions and newspaper headlines. It’s all very unsettling, and sometimes I feel so wound up, I just can’t settle down.

The most perplexing part is that there have been times, at least a couple of weeks here and there, when the deep sadness has lifted, and I've felt a bit more like my old self. But even during those clearer moments, the visions and these strange messages, these 'mind-glimpses' as I call them, they still persist. They haven't gone away, even when the gloom has, proving that this isn't just severe depression.

    B. Schizophrenia

I’ve also been tasting this awful, metallic flavor in my mouth, like old pennies, even when I haven't eaten anything. My face sometimes just… twists, on its own, and I can hear myself saying odd things, like "time chimes, rhymes with crimes." This has been happening for a while, these odd thoughts and tastes, about a year and seven months total. But for most of that time, nearly a year and six months, it’s been the deep sadness and those terrible dreams.
